title: Heat with oil? The evaluators said turn the heat pump off below 8 degrees. A year later, 25.

scenes.purpose: Put the question to the oil-heated viewer before the advice lands.

visual.description: Dark field; the question "Heat with oil?" types on in large type and holds while the advice is spoken.

scenes.direction: Cold open; the question types on with the first words, then holds.
scenes.narration: Heat with oil and own a heat pump? One evaluation's advice: switch the heat pump off on the coldest days and let the oil burner run.

scenes.purpose: Show the two switch-off temperatures side by side, each on its year.

visual.description: Two stat tiles stacked in the portrait frame, 2015 above 2016; each tile's figure lands as it is spoken, 8°F first then 25°F; the note says these are switch-off temperatures, not savings.

chart.title: Switch the heat pump off below
chart.note: Outdoor temperatures below which oil ran cheaper in that year; not a saving figure.

scenes.direction: First tile on "8", second on "25"; hold a beat after the sentence.
scenes.narration: Its switch-off point was 8 degrees Fahrenheit in 2015 and 25 degrees the year after: the outdoor temperature below which oil ran cheaper, not a saving figure.

scenes.purpose: Name what sets the line so the viewer sees why it moved.

visual.description: Three short lines build down the frame as each condition is spoken: oil price, electricity price, cold performance.

scenes.direction: Lines appear on "oil", "electricity" and "performs"; hold on the last.
scenes.narration: The line moved because it is set by that year's oil and electricity prices and by how the heat pump performs in the cold; if oil gets dearer against electricity, the point may move lower.

scenes.purpose: Scope the advice: one evaluation, oil only; propane and resistance went the other way.

visual.description: Three lines build as each fuel is named: oil watches the line, propane and electric resistance go to the heat pump.

scenes.direction: Lines on "oil-heated", "electric resistance" and "propane"; hold after the sentence.
scenes.narration: This is one evaluation of ductless mini-splits in Massachusetts and Rhode Island homes, and the advice is for oil-heated homes only: against electric resistance it found the heat pump nearly always cheaper to run, and against propane, always.

scenes.purpose: The evaluators' own caveat, in their words.

visual.description: Quote card: the evaluators' phrase in quotation marks, the citation naming the source beneath.

scenes.direction: Quote fades in with the sentence; hold a beat.
scenes.narration: The evaluators allowed that not every household wishes to think about which heater to run and when.

scenes.purpose: Leave the viewer with the action and the pointer to the main video.

visual.description: Two lines, one per sentence: the action first, then the pointer to the main video.

scenes.direction: First line with s06, second with s07; hold to the end.
scenes.narration: If you heat with oil, check whether oil or the heat pump runs cheaper at this year's prices before the cold comes, and expect the answer to move. Which homes a heat pump saves money in at all is the full inquiry; see the main video.
